questions.stem: The <u>lowest</u> cast in the Indian society were the
explanation_steps: The four varnas (castes) of ancient India, from top to bottom: Brahmans (priests), Kshatriyas (warriors), Vaishyas (merchants, farmers), Sudras (peasants, labourers).

The textbook: 'At the lowest level of Indian society were the Untouchables. In fact, the Untouchables were not even considered part of the caste system (which is why they are sometimes referred to as outcastes).'

The stem says 'lowest … in the Indian society', which matches the textbook sentence word for word, so the intended answer is B. Strictly, the lowest of the four castes is the Sudras (D), so D is also accepted.
tips: 'Lowest in society' = Untouchables (outcastes); 'lowest of the four varnas' = Sudras. Read which one the question asks.

similar_questions.stem: In ancient Indian society the Kshatriyas were
explanation_steps: The second varna, below the Brahmans, was the Kshatriyas – warriors and rulers.
Answer: B.

textbook_ref.unit: Unit 4 – China and India (3000 B.C.E.–500 C.E.)

questions.review_flag: The paper writes 'cast' for 'caste'. The textbook puts the Untouchables at 'the lowest level of Indian society' but outside the caste system; the lowest of the four castes is the Sudras. Keyed B (textbook wording); D accepted. Teacher decision.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements is <u>wrong</u>?

options.A: On May 2, 1889 the Treaty of Wuchalle was signed.
options.B: Italy was defeated at the Battle of Adwa.
options.C: The Italians were defeated at Halay.
options.D: Mereb-Belesa-Muna line became a border between Italian Eritrea and Ethiopia.

explanation_steps: A is true: 'On May 2, 1889 the Treaty of Wuchale was signed between Italy and the Kingdom of Shawa.'
B and D are true: after the Italian defeat at Adwa (1896) the Treaty of Addis Ababa recognised 'the pre-war Mereb-Belesa-Muna line to be the boundary line between Ethiopia and Italian Eritrea.'

C is wrong: at Halay (December 1894) Bahta Hagos attacked the Italian garrison and caused heavy damage, but Italian reinforcements arrived from Asmara and Massawa; Bahta was wounded and died. The Italians were not defeated. Answer: C.
tips: Halay = Bahta Hagos's revolt (1894), which failed; Adwa = Italian defeat (1896).

similar_questions.stem: The Eritrean leader who revolted against the Italians and died fighting at Halay in 1894 was
explanation_steps: Textbook: 'On December 18, Bahta attacked an Italian army stationed at Halay… Bahta was wounded and later died.'
Answer: B.

textbook_ref.section: 12.1 Italian expansion – Treaty of Wuchale and the Mereb-Belesa-Muna line

questions.stem: One of the following <u>is false</u> about Islam.

options.D: Successors of Mohammed were called Sultans.

explanation_steps: The textbook: after Mohammed's death in 632 his followers chose Abu Bakr 'to be their leader. He was named caliph or successor to Mohammed.'
The successors were caliphs, not sultans (sultan was a later title of Turkish rulers). A, B, C and E are true. Answer: D.
tips: Caliph = 'successor' of the Prophet; the first four were Abu Bakr, Umar, Uthman and Ali.

explanation_steps: The textbook: 'Latin was the most widespread language of the medieval period. Used in the Church and schools, Latin enabled learned people to communicate all over in Europe.'
Vernaculars (Spanish, French, English) only began to be written from the twelfth century. Answer: E.

questions.stem: Which of the following events happened <u>first</u>?

options.B: Germany and Italy sent troops to Spain
options.E: World War Two came into being

explanation_steps: Dates: Italy invaded Ethiopia in October 1935; Germany and Italy sent troops to Spain in 1936; Germany took the Sudetenland (1938) and the rest of Czechoslovakia (March 1939); Germany invaded Poland on 1 September 1939, which started World War II.
The textbook: 'Mussolini invaded Ethiopia from Eritrea and Somalia in 1935… In 1936, both Germany and Italy sent troops to Spain.' Earliest = A.
tips: Order of aggression: Manchuria 1931 → Ethiopia 1935 → Rhineland/Spain 1936 → Austria/Sudetenland 1938 → Czechoslovakia Mar 1939 → Poland Sep 1939.

similar_questions.stem: Which event happened last?

options.C: Hitler sent troops into the Rhineland

explanation_steps: 1931, 1935, 1936, 1938, 1939 – the invasion of Poland (September 1939) was last.
Answer: E.

questions.stem: The <u>first</u> political party to be formed in Eritrea was the
explanation_steps: The textbook: 'The first political party to be founded was the Muslim League (Al Rabita Al Islamiya), which was established in December 1946 in Keren, one month after Wa'ela Biet Giorgis.'
The Unionist Party was formally founded on 21 March 1947; the Liberal Progressive Party (Eritrea for Eritreans) and the Pro-Italy Party came later. Answer: B.

questions.stem: One of the following <u>was not</u> a member of the French Third Estate.
explanation_steps: Old Regime France had three estates: First Estate = the clergy; Second Estate = the nobles; Third Estate = the commoners (peasants, artisans/craftsmen, shopkeepers, merchants, bankers and professionals – the bourgeoisie).
The clergy (upper and lower) belonged to the First Estate. Answer: A.
tips: Clergy = 1st, nobles = 2nd, everyone else (≈97 %) = 3rd Estate.

similar_questions.stem: The largest group within the French Third Estate was the
explanation_steps: Textbook: 'The peasants, who constituted 75 to 80 percent of the total population, were the largest section of the Third Estate.'
Answer: B.

textbook_ref.section: 2.1 The Old Regime – the three estates

questions.stem: Which of the following countries <u>was not</u> affected by the Revolutions of 1848?
explanation_steps: In 1848 revolutions broke out in France, the German states including Prussia, the Austrian Empire (Vienna, Hungary, Prague) and the Italian states.

Britain (England) avoided revolution – it had already reformed Parliament and the Chartist petition of 1848 ended peacefully. Russia also had no revolution; its army helped Austria crush the Hungarians (1849).
Both A and B were unaffected. England is the usual textbook answer, so B is keyed; A is also accepted.
tips: 1848 unrest: France, Germany/Prussia, Austria-Hungary, Italy. Spared: Britain and Russia.

similar_questions.stem: The revolutions of 1848 began in
explanation_steps: Textbook: 'Revolution in France was again the cause for revolution in other countries.' (February 1848)
Answer: B.

textbook_ref.note: The textbook describes the revolutions in France, the German states, Austria and Italy and mentions Russian troops crushing the Hungarians, but does not state which countries escaped revolution.

questions.review_flag: Two options were unaffected: both Britain (England) and Russia escaped the 1848 revolutions. Keyed B (usual answer); A accepted. Teacher decision.

questions.stem: Identify the <u>correct</u> statement.

options.C: The ELM was founded in the Sudan in November 1958.

questions.stem: Post independent Africa faced all of the following challenges, <u>except</u>

questions.stem: If the Nakfa depreciates against the dollar,

options.A: Eritrean export prices in dollar terms will increase.
options.B: the Nakfa price of Eritrean imports will decrease.
options.C: Eritrean export prices in dollar terms will decrease.
options.D: inflation rate in Eritrea will decrease.

explanation_steps: The textbook: the exchange rate is 'the price of one currency in terms of another currency', e.g. 1 USD = Nakfa 15.

Depreciation means one dollar buys more Nakfa (e.g. 1 USD = Nakfa 20). A product priced at Nakfa 300 then costs foreigners 300 ÷ 20 = $15 instead of 300 ÷ 15 = $20 – exports become cheaper in dollars (C).
Imports become dearer in Nakfa (B is false), which tends to raise inflation (D is false). Answer: C.
tips: Weaker home currency → exports cheaper abroad, imports dearer at home.
